q: This is also my first marriage and pregnancy, I’ve done research but it is unrealistic to expect anybody to know fucking everything about pregnancy, about children, about your in laws.
cx: Update post answering strangers who asked why the couple hadn't discussed family visit rules earlier.

q: And yes the conclusion is, my in laws will have to wait for 6 months to see the baby if they don’t wish to get the vaccine.
cx: The visit rule she and her husband agreed for both sets of grandparents.

q: Her mother visits us regularly, and she’s honestly a huge help. She loves spending time with her grandson, and he absolutely adores her too. She even encourages us to take some time for ourselves, go out for dinner, travel for a weekend, etc. while she stays with him.
cx: International couple with a 2-year-old and a second baby coming; grandmother flies in monthly.

q: I appreciate everything she does and I know it comes from love, but I don’t want her taking over the entire household every time she visits.
cx: The same helper also redoes and breaks things around the house.

q: I dont even know how to tell him that I just want him to look up and learn about breastfeeding because I feel like he doesnt understand how hard I am trying.
cx: A week and a half postpartum, she does all nights; husband's comments land as pushback.

q: He moves so slow to help me sometimes and idk if its because he doesnt know what to do or if its because he is waiting for me to explain more of what I want.
cx: On her husband in the first days home.

q: this is a “once in a lifetime experience for him, so can’t I just nut up for one weekend for him?”
cx: Seven weeks after her second birth, husband's reply when she dreads three days alone with a newborn and toddler.

q: The wedding is no kids, so I will be staying home with our girls. Also, my parents will be out of town at the same time for their annual vacation, so I will be totally alone. I have friends, but they aren’t moms so they don’t get it.
cx: Her backup help is away the same weekend.

q: But we planned everything for one, we didn't want a sibling. We have one spare room, one free seat in the car. We wanted to use cloth diapers! We felt so ready to do all the tummy time, skin to skin, no containers, no screentime, all the attention on this one kid!
cx: Expectant father after the 9-week scan shows twins.

q: I am doing my best to handle everything that I can (helping Wife get dressed, helping Wife in/out of bed, waking up every 3 hours to feed baby overnight, handling bottle feeding while Wife breastpumps) and I am very overwhelmed.
cx: First-time father six days after a surgical birth.

q: My Sister has been helping out here and there with laundry, cleaning, baby care, dog care, but she can't be here all the time and I don't have any friends/family nearby other than her to come help out.
cx: Who helps in the first week.

q: He’s already anticipating everyone saying that what matters is a healthy baby. Of course everyone wants a healthy baby, but let’s not diminish grieving what you imagined your family might look like?
cx: Second son on the way; her husband had hoped for a daughter.

q: He was telling us that “he and his wife go on a walk every day” and that “she feels like she hasn’t given birth at all”
cx: A friend's husband pressed her to walk a week after a hard birth; his wife later said she didn't feel fine.

q: I also feel incompetent because I’ve been listening to their blissful pregnancy/birth/parenting for months and my experience is very different.
cx: Friends who gave birth three days apart.

q: what’s stressing me out is that because my MIL is flying in from another country, there’s this added pressure that she’ll be with us all day rather than doing short visits and may want to stay longer than a few days with us.
cx: South Asian or Arab family norms differ between spouses; they bought the mother-in-law a ticket for the birth.

q: we already arranged both a night nurse and a day nurse for the first month, so we don’t really need extra hands.
cx: Paid help is booked; family help would add hosting, not hands.

q: in my culture/background, after a woman gives birth there usually isn’t an expectation to host or have many visitors, even close family. normally only the women closest to her, like her mother or sisters, visit during that period. then after 40 days there’s usually a larger gathering for the family to officially meet the baby.
cx: The visiting custom she grew up with.

q: i feel overwhelmed thinking about having so many people in the apartment after birth. my mom, MIL, day nurse, night nurse. […] my husband doesn’t fully get my perspective. to him, having more people around feels supportive and helpful.
cx: Counting who will be in the flat after the birth.

q: At 25 weeks, we’ve bought 4 outfits. She has bought 30 outfits, 10 bibs, 5 burp rags, 3 blankets, 6 shoes, socks, stuffed animal, hats, books, diaper bag, diapers, wipes, car seat, crib… maybe 25% from a registry we hastily threw together to focus her energy.
cx: Travel nurses who move often keep baby items minimal; the first grandchild's grandmother does not.

q: She rubs my belly without asking, calls my in utero child “my baby”, and has told me when we visit my daughter will sleep in their room with her (LOL, nope). […] We plan on not welcoming any family until a month or so for my own sanity.
cx: Her visit plan for after the birth.

q: They don’t say anything but dismiss him by barely looking at him or acknowledging him.
cx: At 31 weeks, her husband attends nearly every appointment but the practice's staff ignore him.

q: I’m so tired of my kind and loving husband being treated like he doesn’t matter this entire experience. He’s so excited to be a dad and just wants me and his baby to be safe.
cx: She relies on him to answer staff's questions.
